messages:
sara_support: Heads-up — customer_ops reported sudden latency and 503s when hitting eu-west for ~30m. They say requests are being routed to us-east and experiencing 300-800ms extra RTT, plus queued retries. attaching repro they used.
customer_ops: Noticed timeouts and then 503s, then many requests went to us-east and we saw token errors (401) on retries. This started after a traffic bump at 08:12 UTC.
mike_infra: Thanks, digging in. Can you paste 1-2 failing request_ids and a curl repro?
customer_ops: request_id=rc_0a1b2c3d, another rc_0a1b2c4e. repro: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"hello"}'``` We see 503 then fallback to us-east with higher latency.
jenny_prodeng: Checking routing policy logs — looks like eu-west capacity alarm fired and routing-service applied spillover_policy=auto-fallback -> target us-east. Also seeing queue growth on eu-west worker pools (queue_len > 400).
mike_infra: Can confirm from infra metrics: eu-west GPU pool reached soft limit at 08:11:45 and started queuing. Routing circuit breaker triggered at 08:12:02. Logs: ```[08:12:02] routing-service INFO route_request id=rc_0a1b2c3d prefer_region=eu-west resolved_region=us-east reason=capacity_spillover```
leo_oncall: Are tokens getting invalidated during retry? The 401s are concerning if retries use different auth contexts.
customer_ops: 401s show up only when the client retries rapidly and gets routed to a different region — our auth service has per-region token scope, so cross-region retries sometimes fail.
jenny_prodeng: Root cause summary: sudden traffic spike + cold-starts on eu-west -> backlog -> automatic spillover to us-east. Replays/retries from client produced transient 401s because token scope has region hints and some internal auth checks are region-scoped.
mike_infra: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Pin this customer's requests to eu-west (route override) 2) Increase eu-west soft concurrency limit for their org temporarily 3) Advise client to add jitter/exponential backoff on retries to avoid token reuse race. Which do you want?
sara_support: Customer asked for immediate fix to reduce cross-region latency and 401s. Suggest we pin them and bump their dedicated soft cap for 1 hour while we stabilize.
leo_oncall: I'll apply a route override for org:acme-corp -> eu-west and raise soft_limit from 80->140 for 1h. Doing it now. @deploybot please confirm rollout.
deploybot: apply-routing-override org=acme-corp region=eu-west ttl=3600 -> OK
deploybot: adjust-soft-limit org=acme-corp region=eu-west old=80 new=140 ttl=3600 -> OK
mike_infra: Instrumentation note: we'll add a temporary alert for queue_len > 250 with spike-action=page on eu-west pools. Also adding audit log entries for spillover decisions so we can trace customer impact.
jenny_prodeng: Longer-term fixes: - improve cold-start capacity (warm pools) for eu-west - prefer-region routing that respects token-scope to avoid cross-region auth failures - better client-side guidance in docs about backoff and idempotency.
sara_support: Customer_ops — can you validate latency now and confirm 401s have stopped?
customer_ops: Quick sanity check: latency back to normal (~40ms extra to eu-west) and no 401s in the last 5m. I'll run full test suite and report if anything else. Thanks team. :tada:
mike_infra: Follow-up action items: jira INF-3758 (warm-pools eu-west), INF-3759 (routing audit logs), DOC-102 (retry/backoff guidance). Assigning owners.
leo_oncall: Closing immediate incident after 20 minutes of green for this customer. Will monitor metrics for next 6 hours. :white_check_mark:
sara_support: Marking resolved for now — will keep customer informed and link the jira items in the ticket.
customer_ops: Appreciated, will confirm after full test.
